title: Cap. VI Arg. 12: third — singulars as singularly loved; Aquinas on election and dilection
pass_a_gloss: Thirdly, to that which was answered by denying that election extends itself to singular persons as singular, we rejoin that we by no means affirm that this decree regards singulars as singulars, but as singularly loved by God from mere gratuitous benevolence. See Thomas, Part 1, q. 23, art. 4: The predestination of some unto eternal salvation presupposes that God wills their salvation. To which pertain election and dilection: Dilection, inasmuch as he wills to them this good of eternal salvation; Election, inasmuch as he wills this good to some before others. And this dilection is presupposed to election.
pass_b_english: Third: to their denial that election reaches singulars as singulars, we reply we do not claim the decree regards singulars merely as singulars, but as singularly loved by God from mere gratuitous goodwill. So Aquinas (ST 1.23.4): predestination of some to eternal salvation presupposes that God wills their salvation. That involves dilection and election — dilection insofar as he wills them the good of eternal salvation; election insofar as he wills that good to some before others. And dilection is presupposed to election.
source_text: Tertio, ad id quod responsum est negando, electionem sese extendere ad singulares personas qua singulares, regerimus, Nos haud affirmare hoc decretum respicere singulares qua singulares, sed qua singulariter Deo ex mera gratuita benevolentia dilectos. Vide Thomas, part. 1. qu. 23. art. 4: Praedestinatio aliquorum in salutem aeternam praesupponit, quod Deus illorum velit salutem. Ad quod pertinet electio et dilectio: Dilectio, in quantum vult iis hoc bonum salutis aeternae; Electio, in quantum hoc bonum aliquibus prae aliis vult. Et haec dilectio praesupponitur electioni.
